peak.note: This young rosé is at its freshest right now, with bright red berry fruit and crisp acidity from the Grenache and Syrah blend that will gradually soften and lose vibrancy, so it is best enjoyed chilled while still youthful.

As a fresh, entry-level Rhône rosé built on Grenache, Cinsault and Syrah, it is at its most vibrant right now, with bright red berry fruit, crisp acidity and a dry citrusy finish that fade quickly with age, so it should be enjoyed young and chilled.

As a Sangiovese rosato from a hot, drought-affected Tuscan vintage, it is past its brightest youthful phase and is now shifting from fresh red-berry fruit toward softer, more savory and dried-herb notes, so it should be enjoyed soon while the acidity still gives it lift.

This cool-site Riesling is still youthfully tight, with bright citrus and green apple fruit framed by firm acidity, and as it ages the sharp edges will soften while petrol and honeyed stone fruit notes begin to emerge.

This unoaked Okanagan Sauvignon Blanc is in its bright, primary youth, with crisp citrus, grapefruit and green herb notes held in focus by lively acidity, and it is best enjoyed fresh before those vibrant aromatics begin to soften.

This approachable, fruit-forward Chardonnay is drinking at its freshest now, with bright orchard fruit and gentle oak that will slowly soften and lose vibrancy rather than gain complexity, as it is built for early enjoyment rather than long cellaring.

This Okanagan Pinot Gris is in its fresh, youthful phase, with crisp orchard fruit and bright acidity from a warm, ripe growing season that favors immediate enjoyment over long cellaring, as the delicate aromatics will gradually fade into softer, waxier tones.

Grechetto's firm structure and Trebbiano Spoletino's saline, citrus-driven freshness give this Montefalco Bianco a bright, mineral profile in its youth, and while a cooler, rain-affected Umbrian season produced lighter concentration, it should gain subtle almond and honeyed complexity with modest cellaring before the fruit begins to fade.

This Petit Chablis from a generous, ripe-leaning Chardonnay year is showing bright citrus, green apple and chalky minerality that is best enjoyed fresh, as its modest structure and lack of oak mean it will gently soften rather than gain real complexity with extended cellaring.

This crisp, unoaked Pinot Grigio is built for freshness rather than age, so its bright green apple, pear and citrus fruit is at its most vivid right now and will slowly soften and lose its zesty lift with extended bottle time.

This is an everyday, unoaked Pinot Grigio built for freshness, so it is showing its best now with crisp citrus, green apple and light floral notes that will gradually fade rather than evolve, making it a wine to enjoy young and chilled.

Young and aromatically vibrant, with peach, apricot blossom and honeysuckle layered over a fresh, mineral spine from Okanagan's cool nights, and its lush texture should gently deepen toward honeyed, waxy complexity while the acidity keeps it poised.

This Sancerre-neighbouring Loire Sauvignon is in its fresh, vibrant youth, with zesty citrus, gooseberry and flinty minerality still tightly wound, and since it is an unoaked, entry-level style built for immediate pleasure it will gently soften rather than gain complexity, so it is best enjoyed while the aromatics are at their most lively.

The wine is showing vivid citrus, white currant and flinty minerality with a crisp, saline finish, and its bright freshness is best enjoyed while the fruit is still youthful before it softens into a more honeyed, subdued profile.

Bright citrus and green apple fruit with razor-sharp Okanagan acidity currently dominate, while the first hints of petrol and honeyed complexity are just beginning to emerge as the wine slowly knits together in bottle.
This Okanagan red blend from a warm, ripe vintage is showing generous dark fruit and supple tannins now, with the structure to hold and gain some savory complexity but little need for long cellaring.

This is an entry-level high-altitude Pinot Noir built for early enjoyment, so right now it shows bright red cherry and raspberry fruit with fresh acidity and soft tannins, and it will gradually lose its vibrancy rather than gain complexity with extended cellaring.

This Okanagan Cabernet Merlot blend is still youthful, with ripe dark fruit and firm but polished tannins from a warm, generally favorable growing season, and it is just beginning to soften and gain savory, cedar-tinged complexity.

As an entry-level Langhe Nebbiolo made for early enjoyment, it is showing bright cherry, rose petal and a touch of dried herb with firm but approachable tannins that are softening gradually, so it drinks best while the fruit is vivid rather than waiting for the tertiary complexity of its Barolo and Barbaresco cousins.

This Maipo-style Cabernet from a warm, concentrated vintage is still youthful and tightly structured, with ripe dark fruit and firm tannins that need more time in bottle to soften and let cedar and tobacco complexity emerge.

This Okanagan Cabernet Sauvignon is still in its youthful phase, with dense dark fruit and firm structured tannins that are beginning to soften, and it is gaining savory, cedar and tobacco complexity as the oak integrates after a warm, ripe growing season.

Still youthful and firmly structured, this Serralunga Barolo shows tight dark cherry, rose and tar notes with muscular tannins and bright acidity that need further bottle age to soften and unfold into its characteristic savory complexity.

This youthful Crianza is currently showing bright red and dark cherry fruit with supple vanilla and spice from its time in American oak, and as the tannins continue to soften it will gain extra depth and a more savory, leathery complexity.

The oak that dominated its youth is now knitting into the fruit, so the dark cherry and plum are gaining leather, dried herb and sweet spice complexity while the tannins soften toward a more supple, savory finish.

The ripe, concentrated fruit and supple tannins of this warm, dry vintage are beginning to knit together, so the Merlot-led plum and blackberry core is showing more generous and approachable now while the Cabernet and Malbec still provide structure and freshness to carry it forward.

This young, joven-style Tempranillo from Cruz de Alba's Hito label is currently showing vibrant dark cherry, blackberry and a touch of toasty oak, with its firm Ribera tannins gradually softening and the fruit-driven freshness still taking centre stage over any tertiary development.

This Bordeaux-style blend is still in its youthful, fruit-driven phase with supple tannins and bright dark berry, but the structure from the Cabernet components is only beginning to integrate, so a few more years in bottle will bring added savory depth and polish.

Coming from a hot, dry growing season that gave concentrated fruit but sometimes lower acidity, this Sangiovese-led Carmignano with its Cabernet backbone is still tight and youthful, showing dark cherry and plum fruit with firm tannins that need more bottle time to soften and bring forward the savory, earthy complexity.

Still youthful and tightly wound, the dried-cherry, cocoa and spice character is held in check by firm tannins and bright acidity, so the wine is gradually softening and gaining savory, leathery complexity that will reward patience while remaining enjoyable with rich braised dishes.

This warm, dry vintage gave the Similkameen Syrah ripe dark fruit and supple tannins that are now integrating into a savory, peppery profile with early notes of leather and smoked meat, though the structure still has plenty of life ahead.

This is still in its youthful phase, with taut cherry and red plum fruit framed by firm yet ripe tannins and bright acidity from a warm but well-balanced growing season, so it rewards patient cellaring or at least decanting before it softens into more savory, earthy complexity.

This youthful Tignanello from a warm, beautifully balanced Tuscan growing season is still tightly wound, with dark cherry, graphite and cedar fruit wrapped in firm yet polished tannins that need more bottle time to soften and reveal the savory, spiced complexity this wine is known for.

w-mionetto-prosecco-doc-treviso.pitch: This is a light, fresh Italian sparkling wine with lively bubbles and soft fruit. It's an easy, cheerful glass to start the evening or to enjoy with salty, crispy plates, and it's only $15 a glass.
w-mionetto-prosecco-doc-treviso.taste: Light and fresh, with soft fruit and lively bubbles, the way Prosecco usually tastes.
w-mionetto-prosecco-doc-treviso.grape: It's made from Glera, the grape behind Prosecco, which gives a light and easy-drinking sparkling wine.
w-mionetto-prosecco-doc-treviso.place: It comes from Treviso in Veneto, north-east Italy, where the summers are warm and the winters cold, softened by Lake Garda and the Adriatic Sea, and DOC on the label means it follows Italy's official rules for wines named after a place.

dishes.why: The bubbles and freshness cut through the crispy batter and the salt.
A light, fresh sparkling wine is a natural partner for salty, herby nibbles.
The delicate fried sea bass stays the star, and the bubbles keep each bite feeling light.

a special occasion, Champagne by the glass

qs.q: Which description best fits the Mionetto Prosecco DOC Treviso?
opts: Light and fresh, with soft fruit and lively bubbles
Full and rich, with toasty notes and very firm bubbles
Very sweet and syrupy, with honeyed fruit and soft fizz
Bone-dry and lean, with salty notes and almost no fruit
qs.why: Prosecco made from Glera is usually light, fresh and fruity rather than rich, toasty or syrupy.

qs.q: What is the best way to pour the Mionetto Prosecco DOC Treviso?
opts: Well chilled at 6-8°C in a flute, no decanting
Cellar cool at 14-16°C in a large glass, decanted
Room warm at 18-20°C in a tumbler, decanted
Lightly cool at 12-14°C in a red glass, no decanting
qs.why: Sparkling wine like this is at its freshest well chilled, and decanting would only knock out the bubbles.

qs.q: What grape is the Mionetto Prosecco DOC Treviso made from?
qs.why: Glera is the main grape of Prosecco, and it gives the Mionetto its light, easy-drinking style with soft fruit.

qs.q: Which Italian region does the Mionetto Prosecco DOC Treviso come from?
qs.why: Veneto in north-east Italy is home to Prosecco as well as Soave and Amarone, so you can tell guests this glass shares a region with the Giuseppe Campagnola Amarone on our list.

A lean, high-acid Champagne whose bubbles refresh the palate against the salty olives, capers and ham.

glass.why: By the glass it is the one most at home with artichoke, olives and herbs, which can be hard on wine.

avoid.why: Artichoke and capers make tannic reds taste metallic and bitter.

best.why: Pinot Noir's earthy, savoury notes match roasted mushrooms perfectly, and its soft tannins and fresh acidity cut the creamy bianco sauce.
A rounder white whose creamy texture mirrors the bianco sauce and fior di latte, with enough freshness to balance the salty Pecorino.
A grand, earthy Tuscan red whose savoury depth loves mushrooms, and whose acidity and tannin stand up to the bacon add-on.

glass.why: By the glass, mushroom and Pinot Noir is one of the easiest earthy-on-earthy matches.

avoid.why: Its light, sweet, fruity style tastes thin and sugary against the deep, earthy umami of the mushrooms.

best.why: Its touch of sweetness tames the peperoncino heat, and its razor-sharp acidity matches the tomato and cuts the creamy stracciatella.
Its gentle sweetness and cool bubbles soothe the chilli and refresh the palate after the rich, creamy sauce.
A crisp, fruity Champagne rosé whose fine bubbles and acidity lift the creamy vodka sauce and stracciatella.

glass.why: By the glass it is the best fire-extinguisher for the chilli, with the acidity to handle the cream and tomato.

avoid.why: Its firm tannins and high alcohol make the chilli feel hotter and taste harsh against the cream.

best.why: A dry, fresh Provençal-style rosé that matches the tomato's acidity and loves garlic and herb-infused olive oil.
Light and crisp, with enough acidity to match the tomato sauce without overwhelming this simple, cheese-free pizza.
Its zesty acidity meets the tomato, its herbal edge picks up the herb oil, and it is fresh enough to cut the burrata if added.

glass.why: By the glass, dry rosé with tomato, garlic and herbs is a Mediterranean classic.

avoid.why: With no cheese or meat to soften its oaky tannins, the sharp tomato makes it taste harsh and bitter.

cocktails.name: Ciclo Espresso Martini
ingredients: Teremana Blanco or Ketel One Vodka

c-luz-de-pasion.pitch: The Luz de Pasion is bright and tart, with tropical passion fruit and fresh lemon over blanco tequila, plus a light herbal, licorice-like hint from a touch of absinthe. It's perfect for tequila fans who like their drinks sour and fruity with a little adventure.
c-luz-de-pasion.say: Luz de Pasion: LOOS deh pah-see-OHN; Teremana: teh-reh-MAH-nah; Cocchi Rossa: KOH-kee ROH-sah; absinthe: AB-sinth
c-luz-de-pasion.taste: Tart and tropical, with passion fruit and lemon up front, a gentle bittersweet wine note and a faint herbal licorice finish.

explain.means: A blanco tequila, which means clear and unaged, so it tastes fresh and peppery with a hint of agave, the plant tequila is made from.
An Italian red wine flavoured with herbs and spices, which adds a soft bittersweet, fruity depth to the drink.
A very strong herbal spirit that tastes of anise, which is like licorice, so a small amount gives the drink a fragrant herbal note.

dishes.why: The tart passion fruit and lemon work like a squeeze of citrus on the salty, delicate oysters.
The sour, fruity drink cuts through the fried, salty, spicy squid and keeps every bite fresh.

alts.when: wants tequila but fruitier, with a bitter edge and no licorice
no tequila, or something lighter and fizzy

qs.q: What is the base spirit of the Luz de Pasion?
qs.why: The Luz de Pasion is built on Teremana Blanco, an unaged blanco tequila.

qs.q: Which description of the Luz de Pasion is the right one to give a guest?
opts: Sweet and creamy, with rich coffee and vanilla
Smoky and boozy, with honey and citrus
Tart and tropical, with passion fruit, lemon and a faint herbal licorice note
Strong and bitter, with no fruit or citrus at all
qs.why: Passion fruit and lemon make it tart and tropical, and the absinthe adds a light licorice-like herbal note.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Luz de Pasion?
qs.why: Absinthe is on the Luz de Pasion's line; the others belong to the Dr. Mario, Strawberry Fields and Silk & Stone Martini.

qs.q: What does the absinthe bring to the Luz de Pasion?
qs.why: Absinthe is an anise-flavoured herbal spirit, so even a little gives a fragrant licorice-like note.

qs.q: A guest who loves tequila wants something tart and tropical with a herbal twist. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Luz de Pasion pairs blanco tequila with tart passion fruit and lemon, and the absinthe gives it the herbal twist.

qs.q: Both the Luz de Pasion and the Strawberry Fields are blanco tequila signatures. Which ingredient is in the Luz de Pasion?
qs.why: Cocchi Rossa is in the Luz de Pasion, while Campari, Licor 43 and aromatic bitters are all in the Strawberry Fields.

c-flora-fizz.pitch: The Flora Fizz is light, bubbly and refreshing, with Ketel One vodka, fresh lime, cranberry and our house-made rosé syrup, topped with soda. It's great for anyone who wants something easy-drinking, fruity and not too strong.
c-flora-fizz.say: Ketel One: KET-ul WUN; rosé: roh-ZAY
c-flora-fizz.taste: Light and fizzy, with tart lime and cranberry balanced by a soft, fruity sweetness.

explain.means: A sweet syrup made here in-house with a rosé flavour, which gives the drink its sweetness and a soft, fruity note.
Soda water, plain fizzy water, which adds bubbles and makes the drink lighter and more refreshing.

dishes.why: The bubbles and tart lime cut through the fried, salty squid and refresh the palate.
The light, tart-sweet fizz matches the salad's tangy dressing and balances the creamy goat cheese.

alts.when: wants bubbles from sparkling wine instead of soda
wants a stronger, less sweet vodka drink

qs.q: What is the base spirit of the Flora Fizz?
qs.why: The Flora Fizz is made with Ketel One Vodka.

qs.q: Which description of the Flora Fizz is the right one to give a guest?
opts: Light, fizzy and tart-sweet, with lime and cranberry
Rich and bitter, strong and stirred, with no citrus
Smoky and spicy, with a salt rim
qs.why: Lime and cranberry give it tartness, the rosé syrup sweetens it, and soda makes it light and fizzy.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Flora Fizz?
qs.why: Cranberry is on the Flora Fizz's line; the others come from the Summer Blush, Paradise Spritz and La Vita Colada.

qs.q: What does the soda do in the Flora Fizz?
opts: Adds bubbles and lightens the drink
Adds a silky foam on top
qs.why: Soda is plain fizzy water, so it adds bubbles and makes the drink lighter.

qs.q: A guest wants a light, refreshing vodka drink with lime and cranberry that isn't too strong. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Flora Fizz is Ketel One vodka with fresh lime, cranberry and soda, so it's light, tart and easy-drinking.

qs.q: Both the Flora Fizz and the Rose Alla Fragola are vodka drinks. Which of these is in the Flora Fizz and not in the Rose Alla Fragola?
qs.why: The Flora Fizz uses fresh lime juice, while lemon juice, Cointreau and strawberry syrup are all in the Rose Alla Fragola.

c-the-pear-se.pitch: The Pear Se, created by Todd Zimmerman, is soft and juicy, with gin, a cognac pear liqueur and pear purée, freshened with lemon and a hint of rosemary. It's ideal for gin lovers who want something fruity and smooth rather than bitter.
c-the-pear-se.say: The Pear Se: PAIR SAY; Belle de Brillet: BELL duh bree-YAY; Cognac: KOHN-yak; purée: pyoo-RAY
c-the-pear-se.taste: Smooth, juicy pear with a fresh squeeze of lemon and a light herbal rosemary note.

explain.means: A French pear liqueur blended with cognac, a French brandy, which adds rich, ripe pear flavour and a little warmth.
Pear blended until smooth, which gives the drink a juicy, fuller body and fresh fruit taste.
A very concentrated rosemary extract used in tiny amounts, which adds a fragrant, piney herbal note.

dishes.why: The juicy pear in the drink echoes the pear on this pizza and balances the salty gorgonzola.
The soft, fruity sweetness is a lovely contrast to the salty cured meats and rich cheeses.

alts.when: wants a gin drink with berry, red wine and a silky texture
wants something lighter and bubbly

qs.q: What is the base spirit of The Pear Se?
qs.why: The Pear Se is built on Seventh Heaven Gin, with the cognac liqueur adding depth.

qs.q: Which description of The Pear Se is the right one to give a guest?
opts: Strong and bitter, with no fruit
Tart and tropical, with a licorice finish
Smooth and juicy, with lemon and a light herbal note
qs.why: Pear purée and pear liqueur make it smooth and juicy, lemon freshens it, and rosemary tincture adds the herbal note.

qs.q: Which of these is in The Pear Se?
qs.why: Belle de Brillet is in The Pear Se; Tia Maria, Chambord and Giffard Pêche belong to the espresso martini and the sangrias.

qs.q: What does the rosemary tincture do in The Pear Se?
opts: Adds a concentrated herbal, piney note in tiny amounts
qs.why: A tincture is a very concentrated extract, so a tiny amount gives a fragrant rosemary note.

qs.q: A gin lover wants something fruity, smooth and gently sweet, with no wine, no bubbles and no egg. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Pear Se is fruity gin with no wine, bubbles or egg, unlike the Blue Rose, Summer Blush or the bitter Negroni with vermouth.

qs.q: Both The Pear Se and the Blue Rose are gin signatures with lemon and rosemary. Which gin is in The Pear Se?
qs.why: The Pear Se uses Seventh Heaven Gin, while the Blue Rose uses Roku Gin.

c-blue-rose.pitch: The Blue Rose, created by Lukas Purm, mixes Japanese Roku Gin with our house blueberry rosemary syrup, a splash of Cabernet Sauvignon and lemon, with egg whites for a silky, foamy texture. It's perfect for guests who love both gin and red wine and want something fruity and smooth.
c-blue-rose.say: Roku: ROH-koo; Cabernet Sauvignon: ka-ber-NAY so-vin-YOHN
c-blue-rose.taste: Tart berry and lemon with a dry red-wine edge, a hint of rosemary and a soft, silky texture.

explain.means: A Japanese gin, which brings a clean, fragrant, lightly floral base.
A sweet syrup made here in-house from blueberry and rosemary, which gives the drink its berry sweetness and herbal note.
A full-bodied red wine, which adds dark fruit and a dry, grippy edge.
Egg whites give the drink a silky, foamy texture; always tell guests with egg allergies or vegan guests.

dishes.why: The red wine and rosemary in the drink match the herby, charred, rich lamb.
The tart berry and dry wine edge cut through the salty, rich meats and cheese.

alts.when: wants gin without egg or wine
wants something more wine-forward

qs.q: What is the base spirit of the Blue Rose?
qs.why: The Blue Rose is built on Roku Gin, a Japanese gin.

qs.q: Which description of the Blue Rose is the right one to give a guest?
opts: Tart berry and lemon with a dry red-wine edge and a silky texture
Light and fizzy, with lime and cranberry
Smoky and spicy, with a salt rim
Strong and bitter, with no fruit or citrus
qs.why: Blueberry syrup and lemon make it tart and fruity, Cabernet adds a dry wine edge, and egg whites make it silky.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Blue Rose?
qs.why: The Blue Rose uses Cabernet Sauvignon; Malbec and Chardonnay-Chenin blanc are in the sangrias and Prosecco is in the spritzes.

qs.q: What do the egg whites do in the Blue Rose?
opts: Give it a silky, foamy texture
qs.why: Egg whites create a silky foam, which is also why you must mention them to guests with egg allergies or vegan guests.

qs.q: A guest who drinks gin but also loves red wine wants something fruity and silky to go with the Fire-Charred Lamb Chops. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Blue Rose combines gin with Cabernet Sauvignon, berry and a silky texture, and its rosemary suits the herby lamb.

qs.q: Both the Blue Rose and The Pear Se are gin signatures with rosemary. What brings the rosemary into the Blue Rose?
qs.why: The Blue Rose gets its rosemary from the house blueberry rosemary syrup, while The Pear Se uses a rosemary tincture.

c-strawberry-fields.pitch: Strawberry Fields is fruity and bright, with ripe strawberry and fresh lime, a soft vanilla sweetness from Licor 43 and a gentle bitter finish from Campari. It's perfect for tequila fans and anyone who likes a fruity drink that isn't too sugary.
c-strawberry-fields.say: El Tequileño: el teh-kee-LEN-yoh; Licor 43: lee-KOR kwah-REN-tah ee TRESS; Campari: kahm-PAH-ree
c-strawberry-fields.taste: Sweet strawberry and tangy lime, softened by vanilla and citrus, with a light bitter edge at the end.

explain.means: A sweet Spanish liqueur that tastes of vanilla and citrus, and it adds a smooth, rounded sweetness to the drink.
A bright red, bitter Italian aperitivo (a drink meant to wake up your appetite before a meal), and it gives the drink a pleasant bitter-orange finish.
A strong herbal and spice flavouring used a few drops at a time, and it adds depth and balance to the drink.
A blanco tequila, meaning a clear, unaged tequila with a fresh agave taste.

dishes.why: The juicy strawberry and lime cool down the spicy, smoky potatoes.
The fruit and the bitter finish cut through the creamy burrata and salty salami.

alts.when: tequila and berry flavour but no bitterness, in a margarita style
lighter and bubbly, with the same Campari bitter edge

qs.q: What is the base spirit in the Strawberry Fields?
qs.why: The Strawberry Fields is built on El Tequileño Blanco, which is a blanco tequila.

qs.q: A guest asks what the Strawberry Fields tastes like. Which description is right?
opts: Dry, strong and bitter, with no fruit at all
Fruity strawberry and lime, softened by vanilla, with a light bitter finish
Rich coffee and caramel, sweet and smooth
Smoky, salty and sharp with blood orange
qs.why: Strawberry syrup and lime give the fruit, Licor 43 adds vanilla, and Campari adds a gentle bitter finish.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Strawberry Fields?
qs.why: The Strawberry Fields has Campari. The other three come from other cocktails on the list.

qs.q: What does the Licor 43 add to the Strawberry Fields?
opts: A sweet vanilla and citrus softness
qs.why: Licor 43 is a Spanish liqueur that tastes of vanilla and citrus, so it rounds out the drink.

qs.q: A guest who loves tequila wants something fruity with a gentle bitter edge, not too sugary. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Strawberry Fields pairs blanco tequila and fruit with Campari for a light bitter finish.

qs.q: The Strawberry Fields and the Red Velvet both use El Tequileño Blanco. What does the Strawberry Fields have that the Red Velvet does not?
opts: Black salt and house raspberry syrup
qs.why: Campari and Licor 43 are only in the Strawberry Fields. The Red Velvet uses Cointreau, raspberry syrup, agave and black salt.

c-la-vita-colada.pitch: La Vita Colada is a tropical rum drink with pineapple and coconut water. It's made silky and clear instead of heavy, and it's finished with a Glenfiddich 15-Year whisky foam. It's great for anyone who loves a piña colada but wants something lighter and smoother.
c-la-vita-colada.say: Flor de Caña: flor deh KAHN-yah; Glenfiddich: glen-FID-ik
c-la-vita-colada.taste: Tropical pineapple and coconut, light and silky rather than creamy, with a soft whisky note from the foam on top.

explain.means: Milk is added to the drink so it curdles, and then the solids are strained out, which leaves a clear, extra-smooth, silky drink with no milky taste.
A foam on top of the drink flavoured with Glenfiddich 15-Year, a single malt Scotch whisky, and it adds a soft, fruity, honeyed whisky aroma.
A rum from Nicaragua, and it's the main spirit in the drink.
The clear, light liquid from inside a coconut, and it gives coconut flavour without the heaviness of cream.

dishes.why: The cool pineapple and coconut freshen the palate after the salty, spicy fried squid.
The tropical sweetness balances the smoky, spicy chorizo.

alts.when: pineapple and coconut but with tequila, in a margarita style
rum and pineapple but lighter and bubbly, with a bitter edge

qs.q: What is the base spirit in La Vita Colada?
qs.why: La Vita Colada is built on Flor de Caña Rum. The Glenfiddich only appears in the foam on top.

qs.q: A guest asks what La Vita Colada tastes like. Which description is right?
opts: Bitter, herbal and strong, with no fruit
Tart lime and salt with smoky heat
Tropical pineapple and coconut, light and silky, with a soft whisky note on top
qs.why: Pineapple juice and coconut water give the tropical taste, milk clarification makes it silky, and the Glenfiddich foam adds a whisky note.

qs.q: Which of these is in La Vita Colada?
qs.why: La Vita Colada uses coconut water. Coconut reduction, pineapple cordial and blood orange syrup belong to other cocktails on the list.

qs.q: What does the milk clarification do to La Vita Colada?
opts: It makes the drink thick and creamy like a milkshake
It makes the drink clear and silky smooth
qs.why: The milk curdles and is strained out, which leaves a clear, smooth drink instead of a creamy one.

qs.q: A guest who likes rum wants a tropical, pineapple-forward drink that's smooth and silky, not bubbly and not heavy or creamy. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: La Vita Colada is rum with pineapple and coconut water, clarified so it's silky and light, and it has no bubbles.

qs.q: La Vita Colada and the Costa Coco both bring pineapple and coconut. Which of these is true of La Vita Colada?
opts: It's rum-based, with a Glenfiddich 15-Year foam
It's made with Cointreau and coconut reduction
qs.why: La Vita Colada uses Flor de Caña Rum and a Glenfiddich foam. The Costa Coco is Patron Blanco tequila with Cointreau, coconut reduction and Tajín.

c-ciclo-espresso-martini.pitch: Our Ciclo Espresso Martini is bold espresso with coffee liqueur, a vanilla touch from Licor 43, brown-sugar sweetness and a hint of orange from Grand Marnier. It's ideal for coffee lovers and after dinner, and you can have it with vodka or with tequila.
c-ciclo-espresso-martini.say: Teremana: teh-reh-MAH-nah; Tia Maria: TEE-ah mah-REE-ah; Licor 43: lee-KOR kwah-REN-tah ee TRESS; Grand Marnier: grahn mar-NYAY; demerara: dem-er-AIR-ah
c-ciclo-espresso-martini.taste: Bold, rich coffee, sweet with vanilla and brown sugar, and a light hint of orange.

explain.means: A sweet coffee liqueur that deepens the coffee flavour and adds sweetness.
A sweet Spanish liqueur that tastes of vanilla and citrus, and it adds a smooth vanilla note.
A syrup made from demerara, a light brown cane sugar, and it gives a toffee-like sweetness.
A 'wash' means only a light touch of Grand Marnier (an orange liqueur made with Cognac) is used, so it adds a hint of orange rather than a full pour.

dishes.why: The sweet, creamy mascarpone and the bold coffee are a natural after-dinner match.
The vanilla and brown-sugar notes in the drink suit the rich, sweet pudding.

alts.when: something stronger and less sweet after dinner
tequila and Licor 43 but fruity instead of coffee

qs.q: Which base spirit can a guest choose for the Ciclo Espresso Martini?
qs.why: The Ciclo Espresso Martini comes with either Teremana Blanco tequila or Ketel One Vodka.

qs.q: A guest asks what the Ciclo Espresso Martini tastes like. Which description is right?
opts: Bold coffee, sweet with vanilla and brown sugar, and a hint of orange
Tart and fruity with strawberry and a bitter finish
Dry, savoury and briny with olives
qs.why: Espresso and Tia Maria give the coffee, Licor 43 and demerara syrup the sweetness, and the Grand Marnier wash the orange hint.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Ciclo Espresso Martini?
qs.why: The Ciclo Espresso Martini has Tia Maria. The other three come from other cocktails on the list.

qs.q: What does the Grand Marnier wash add to the Ciclo Espresso Martini?
opts: A hint of orange and Cognac
qs.why: Grand Marnier is an orange liqueur made with Cognac, and a wash means only a light touch of it is used.

qs.q: A guest wants an after-dinner coffee cocktail but prefers tequila to vodka. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Ciclo Espresso Martini is a coffee cocktail that can be made with Teremana Blanco tequila.

qs.q: The Ciclo Espresso Martini and the Strawberry Fields both contain Licor 43. What sets the Ciclo Espresso Martini apart?
opts: Espresso and Tia Maria Coffee Liqueur
qs.why: Only the Ciclo Espresso Martini has espresso and Tia Maria. Campari, bitters, strawberry syrup and lime belong to the Strawberry Fields.

c-the-old-fashioned.pitch: Our Old Fashioned is strong and smooth. The whisky is washed with brown butter, so it tastes nutty and rich, with warm spice from Angostura and a touch of orange bitters. It's the one for whisky lovers who want a classic, spirit-forward drink with a twist.
c-the-old-fashioned.taste: Strong, smooth whisky with a nutty, buttery richness, warm spice and a hint of orange.

explain.means: The whisky is mixed with melted brown butter, then the butter is chilled and strained out, which leaves a nutty, buttery flavour and a smoother feel with no butter in the glass.
A famous aromatic bitters, which is a strong spice-and-herb flavouring used a few drops at a time, and it adds warm spice and depth.
A strong orange-peel flavouring used in drops, and it adds a bright orange note.

dishes.why: The strong, nutty whisky stands up to the charred, rich steak.
The brown-butter nuttiness matches the earthy, salty truffle.

alts.when: whisky but smoky, with honey and citrus
just as strong but bitter, with gin instead of whisky

qs.q: What is the base spirit in The Old Fashioned?
qs.why: The Old Fashioned is built on brown butter-washed Traveller Whisky.

qs.q: A guest asks what The Old Fashioned tastes like. Which description is right?
opts: Strong and smooth, nutty and buttery, with warm spice and orange
Sweet, tart and berry-forward with salt
qs.why: Brown butter-washed whisky with Angostura and orange bitters makes a strong, nutty, spiced drink.

qs.q: Which of these is in The Old Fashioned?
qs.why: The Old Fashioned has Angostura. The other three come from other cocktails on the list.

qs.q: What does the brown butter wash do to the whisky in The Old Fashioned?
opts: It gives a nutty, buttery flavour and a smoother feel, with no butter left in the glass
It makes the whisky smoky like a peated Scotch
It adds sweetness like a syrup
It adds a bright orange aroma
qs.why: The butter's flavour stays in the whisky, but the fat is chilled and strained out.

qs.q: A guest wants a strong, spirit-forward whisky drink that isn't smoky. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Old Fashioned is a strong whisky drink with nutty, spiced flavours. The Dr. Mario has smoky Laphroaig.

qs.q: The Old Fashioned and the Dr. Mario are both whisky cocktails. Which of these is true of The Old Fashioned?
opts: It uses Johnnie Walker Black and Laphroaig
It uses brown butter-washed Traveller Whisky with Angostura and orange bitters
It has honey syrup and clarified citrus
It has Lillet Blanc and olives
qs.why: The Old Fashioned is Traveller Whisky with bitters. The Dr. Mario uses Johnnie Walker Black, Laphroaig, honey syrup and clarified citrus.

c-the-negroni.pitch: The Negroni is a classic bitter cocktail: bold and boozy, with a gentle herbal sweetness from the vermouth. It's perfect for anyone who likes their drinks strong, bittersweet and not fruity, and it makes a great before-dinner drink.
c-the-negroni.say: Roku: ROH-koo. Campari: kahm-PAH-ree. Vermouth: ver-MOOTH.
c-the-negroni.taste: Strong and bitter with a soft, herbal sweetness and a bitter-orange edge.

explain.means: A Japanese gin made with Japanese botanicals such as yuzu (a Japanese citrus), sakura (cherry blossom) and green tea, so it gives the drink a bright, slightly floral base.
A bright red Italian bitter liqueur with bitter orange and herbal flavours, and it's what makes the Negroni taste bitter.
A red wine that has been strengthened with extra alcohol, sweetened and flavoured with herbs and spices, and it softens the bitterness with a rich, herbal sweetness.

dishes.why: The bitterness cuts right through the salty, rich cured meats and cheese, so each bite feels fresh again.
Salty, herby olives and a bitter Negroni are a natural before-dinner match.

alts.when: lighter, bubbly and less boozy, but still with a Campari bitter edge
sweeter and fruitier, with just a touch of Campari

qs.q: What is the base spirit of The Negroni?
qs.why: The Negroni is built on Roku Gin.

qs.q: A guest asks what The Negroni tastes like. Which description is right?
opts: Sweet and fruity, with bright lime sourness
Strong and bitter, with a soft herbal sweetness
Smoky and honeyed, with a gentle sour lift
qs.why: Campari makes it bitter, sweet vermouth adds herbal sweetness, and there is no juice in it.

qs.q: Which of these is in The Negroni?
qs.why: The Negroni is Roku Gin, Campari and sweet vermouth.

qs.q: Which ingredient gives The Negroni its bitter edge?
qs.why: Campari is a bitter Italian liqueur and the source of the Negroni's bitterness.

qs.q: A guest wants a strong, bittersweet drink before dinner and says nothing fruity or bubbly. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Negroni is strong and bitter, with no fruit juice and no bubbles.

qs.q: The Negroni and the Paradise Spritz both contain Campari. Which ingredient is in the Paradise Spritz but not in The Negroni?
qs.why: The Paradise Spritz is topped with Prosecco and soda, so it is lighter and bubbly, while the Negroni has no bubbles.

c-silk-stone-martini.pitch: The Silk & Stone Martini is a smooth, dry vodka martini with a savoury olive-oil richness and a soft hint of orange. It's ideal for anyone who loves a classic dirty or olive martini and wants something extra silky.
c-silk-stone-martini.say: Lillet Blanc: lee-LAY BLAHN. EVOO: say each letter, E-V-O-O, which stands for extra virgin olive oil.
c-silk-stone-martini.taste: Smooth, dry and savoury, with olive flavour, a silky feel and a light touch of orange.

explain.means: A 'wash' means the vodka has been mixed with extra virgin olive oil and the oil taken back out, which leaves the olive flavour and a silkier feel without any oiliness.
A French aperitif wine (a wine-based drink meant to be sipped before a meal), made from white wine and citrus liqueurs, which adds a light, slightly sweet, orangey softness.
A few drops of a strong orange-and-spice flavouring that adds a hint of orange peel aroma rather than real bitterness.

dishes.why: The salty, delicate oysters go beautifully with a clean, savoury olive martini.
Salty, rich caviar and an ice-cold, silky vodka martini are a classic match.

alts.when: wants something stirred and strong but more bitter
wants a martini that's sweeter, with coffee

qs.q: What is the base spirit of the Silk & Stone Martini?
qs.why: The Silk & Stone Martini is made with Grey Goose, a vodka.

qs.q: A guest asks what the Silk & Stone Martini tastes like. Which description is right?
opts: Dry, silky and savoury, with olive and a soft hint of orange
Strong and bitter, with a sweet herbal edge
Tart and fruity, with fresh lime
qs.why: Olive oil-washed vodka, Lillet Blanc, orange bitters and olives make it dry, savoury and silky.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Silk & Stone Martini?
qs.why: The Silk & Stone Martini uses Lillet Blanc alongside the olive oil-washed Grey Goose.

qs.q: What does the EVOO wash do to the Grey Goose in the Silk & Stone Martini?
opts: Gives it olive oil flavour and a silkier feel
Adds a light orange liqueur aroma
Makes it crystal clear by removing cloudiness
qs.why: Washing the vodka with extra virgin olive oil leaves olive flavour and a smoother, silkier texture.

qs.q: A guest who loves olives wants a dry, savoury martini but doesn't drink gin. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Silk & Stone Martini is a dry, savoury vodka martini with olive oil and olives.

qs.q: The Silk & Stone Martini and the Ciclo Espresso Martini can both be made with vodka. Which description fits the Silk & Stone Martini?
opts: Dry and savoury, with olive oil and olives
Bitter and red, with sweet vermouth
qs.why: The Silk & Stone Martini is dry and savoury, while the Ciclo Espresso Martini is sweeter, with coffee liqueur and espresso.

c-dr-mario.pitch: The Dr. Mario is a smoky Scotch cocktail sweetened with honey and brightened with citrus, so it's smooth, warming and a little tart. It's perfect for whisky lovers, especially anyone who enjoys a peaty, smoky Scotch.
c-dr-mario.taste: Smoky and honeyed, with a gentle sour lift from the citrus.

explain.means: A smooth blended Scotch whisky that gives the drink a rich, slightly smoky backbone.
A single malt Scotch whisky from the island of Islay, famous for its big, peaty smoke (peat is a fuel that gives whisky a smoky, earthy taste), and it's what makes the drink smoky.
Honey thinned into a syrup so it mixes easily, which adds a soft, floral sweetness.
Citrus juice that has been made clear by removing the pulp and cloudiness, so it adds sourness while keeping the drink smooth and clear.

dishes.why: The smoky, spicy chorizo matches the smoke in the whisky, and the honey calms the heat.
Charred, rich lamb loves a smoky Scotch drink with a bit of citrus to keep it fresh.

alts.when: wants smoky but fruitier, with mezcal instead of whisky
wants whisky that's stronger, with no citrus

qs.q: What is the base spirit of the Dr. Mario?
qs.why: The Dr. Mario is made with Johnnie Walker Black and Laphroaig, both Scotch whiskies.

qs.q: A guest asks what the Dr. Mario tastes like. Which description is right?
opts: Smoky and honeyed, with a gentle sour lift
Strong and bitter, with a herbal sweetness
Dry, silky and savoury, with olive
qs.why: Smoky Scotch, honey syrup and clarified citrus make it smoky, sweet and a little tart.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Dr. Mario?
qs.why: The Dr. Mario is sweetened with honey syrup.

qs.q: Which ingredient gives the Dr. Mario its big smoky character?
qs.why: Laphroaig is a peaty Islay Scotch, famous for its smoke.

qs.q: A guest who loves smoky Scotch wants a cocktail that's a little sweet and a little sour. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Dr. Mario combines smoky Laphroaig with honey syrup and clarified citrus.

qs.q: The Dr. Mario and The Old Fashioned are both whisky cocktails. Which ingredient is in the Dr. Mario but not in The Old Fashioned?
qs.why: The Dr. Mario has clarified citrus for a sour lift, while The Old Fashioned has no citrus juice.

c-summer-blush.pitch: The Summer Blush is a light, bubbly spritz with floral elderflower, juicy white peach and a squeeze of lemon. It's great for anyone who wants something refreshing and easy-drinking that isn't too boozy.
c-summer-blush.taste: Light and bubbly, with floral elderflower, soft white peach and a little lemony tartness.

explain.means: An elderflower-flavoured gin from Empress 1908, which gives the drink its floral, perfumed taste.
A light, fruity Italian sparkling wine that adds bubbles and freshness.
A light, bubbly drink topped up with sparkling wine and/or soda water, made for easy sipping.

dishes.why: A delicate, herby green salad suits a light, floral spritz that won't overpower it.
The bubbles and lemon refresh the palate after delicate fried sea bass.

alts.when: wants a fruitier strawberry spritz, made with vodka instead of gin
wants a spritz with a bitter Campari edge

qs.q: What is the base spirit of the Summer Blush?
qs.why: The Summer Blush is built on Empress Elderflower, a gin.

qs.q: A guest asks what the Summer Blush tastes like. Which description is right?
opts: Strong and bitter, with a herbal sweetness
Light and bubbly, with floral elderflower and soft peach
Smoky and honeyed, with a sour lift
Dry, silky and savoury, with olive
qs.why: Elderflower gin, white peach, lemon, Prosecco and soda make it light, floral and bubbly.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Summer Blush?
qs.why: The Summer Blush uses white peach with the elderflower gin.

qs.q: Which ingredient gives the Summer Blush its floral character?
qs.why: Empress Elderflower is an elderflower gin, and it's what makes the drink floral.

qs.q: A guest wants something light, bubbly and not too boozy for a sunny afternoon, with no bitterness. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Summer Blush is a light, floral spritz with no bitter Campari.

qs.q: The Summer Blush and the Rose Alla Fragola are both spritzes. The Rose Alla Fragola leans on strawberry. Which fruit leads the Summer Blush?
qs.why: The Summer Blush is built around white peach, while the Rose Alla Fragola uses strawberry syrup.

c-rose-alla-fragola.pitch: The Rose Alla Fragola is a light, sweet-tart sparkler: Grey Goose vodka with strawberry, lemon and orange liqueur, topped with sparkling rosé wine and rose lemonade. It's perfect for anyone who loves fruity, bubbly drinks and doesn't want anything bitter or too boozy.
c-rose-alla-fragola.say: Rose Alla Fragola: rose AH-lah FRAH-goh-lah ('fragola' is Italian for strawberry); Cointreau: KWAN-troh; Mionetto: mee-oh-NET-oh
c-rose-alla-fragola.taste: Sweet strawberry and bright lemon with a hint of orange, made light and fizzy by sparkling rosé and rose lemonade.

explain.means: A drink topped with sparkling wine and/or something fizzy, which keeps it light, bubbly and easy to sip.
A clear French orange liqueur that adds a sweet orange note.
A sparkling rosé wine from Mionetto, an Italian sparkling wine maker; it gives the drink its pink bubbles.
Lemonade flavoured with rose; it adds a floral touch and a sweet-tart lift.

dishes.why: The sweet strawberry and bubbles play nicely off the creamy burrata and salty salami.
Light, lemony bubbles are a refreshing match for salty, delicate oysters.

alts.when: less sweet, with a bitter edge
another vodka drink, with soda instead of sparkling wine

qs.q: What is the base spirit in the Rose Alla Fragola?
qs.why: The Rose Alla Fragola is built on Grey Goose, which is a vodka.

qs.q: How would you describe the taste of the Rose Alla Fragola to a guest?
opts: Sweet-tart and fruity, with strawberry and lemon, light and bubbly
Bittersweet and tropical, with pineapple, blood orange and a bitter red liqueur
Smoky and tangy, with blood orange, lime and a touch of salt
Strong and spirit-forward, with smoky Scotch and honey
qs.why: Strawberry syrup, lemon juice, sparkling rosé and rose lemonade make it sweet-tart, fruity and fizzy with no bitterness.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Rose Alla Fragola?
qs.why: Cointreau, an orange liqueur, is on the Rose Alla Fragola's list; the others belong to other cocktails.

qs.q: In the Rose Alla Fragola, which ingredient does the Italian word 'Fragola' in the name point to?
qs.why: 'Fragola' is Italian for strawberry, and strawberry syrup gives the drink its main fruit flavour.

qs.q: A guest wants something light, bubbly and fruity with strawberry, and says they like vodka. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Rose Alla Fragola is Grey Goose vodka with strawberry, topped with sparkling rosé and rose lemonade.

qs.q: What is the difference between the Rose Alla Fragola and the Summer Blush?
opts: The Rose Alla Fragola has vodka, strawberry and sparkling rosé; the Summer Blush has Empress Elderflower, white peach and Prosecco
The Rose Alla Fragola has Empress Elderflower and white peach; the Summer Blush has vodka and strawberry
The Rose Alla Fragola has rum and Campari; the Summer Blush has vodka and strawberry
The Rose Alla Fragola has Prosecco and soda; the Summer Blush has sparkling rosé and rose lemonade
qs.why: Both are spritzes with lemon, but the Rose Alla Fragola is vodka, strawberry and sparkling rosé, while the Summer Blush is Empress Elderflower, white peach and Prosecco.

c-paradise-spritz.pitch: The Paradise Spritz is bittersweet and tropical: Appleton Estate rum with pineapple, blood orange and lime, a splash of bitter Campari, and Prosecco and soda on top. It's great for guests who like an Aperol- or Campari-style spritz but want a sunny, fruity twist.
c-paradise-spritz.taste: Juicy pineapple and blood orange with tangy lime and a pleasant bitter edge, all light and bubbly.

explain.means: A bright red Italian bitter liqueur, a classic aperitivo (a before-dinner drink meant to wake up your appetite), which gives this drink its bittersweet orange edge.
A sweet, concentrated pineapple syrup that adds tropical fruit and sweetness.
A red-fleshed orange with a sweet, slightly berry-like taste.
An Italian sparkling white wine that tops the drink and makes it light and fizzy.

dishes.why: The fruity, bittersweet bubbles cool down the smoky, spicy chorizo.
Bubbles and lime cut through the fried squid, and the fruit balances its salt and spice.

alts.when: something stronger with the same bitter Campari edge
sweeter and fruitier, with no bitterness

qs.q: What is the base spirit in the Paradise Spritz?
qs.why: The Paradise Spritz is built on Appleton Estate, which is a rum.

qs.q: How would you describe the taste of the Paradise Spritz to a guest?
opts: Bittersweet and tropical, with pineapple and blood orange, light and bubbly
Sweet and fruity, with strawberry and pink bubbles and no bitterness
Smoky and tangy, with blood orange, lime and a touch of salt
Strong and spirit-forward, bitter, with gin and sweet vermouth
qs.why: Pineapple, blood orange and lime bring the fruit, Campari adds the bitterness, and Prosecco and soda make it light and fizzy.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Paradise Spritz?
qs.why: Pineapple cordial is on the Paradise Spritz's list; the others belong to other cocktails.

qs.q: In the Paradise Spritz, which ingredient adds the bitter edge?
qs.why: Campari is a bitter Italian liqueur and the only one of these in the Paradise Spritz.

qs.q: A guest loves Campari but wants something light, bubbly and tropical rather than strong. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Paradise Spritz has Campari with pineapple and blood orange, topped with Prosecco and soda.

qs.q: What is the difference between the Paradise Spritz and the Summer Blush?
opts: The Paradise Spritz has rum, Campari, pineapple and blood orange; the Summer Blush has Empress Elderflower and white peach
The Paradise Spritz has Empress Elderflower and white peach; the Summer Blush has rum and Campari
The Paradise Spritz has vodka and strawberry; the Summer Blush has rum and Campari
The Paradise Spritz has sparkling rosé; the Summer Blush has Campari and pineapple
qs.why: Both are topped with Prosecco and soda, but only the Paradise Spritz has rum, bitter Campari and tropical fruit.

c-brasa-roja-mezcal.pitch: The Brasa-Roja Mezcal is a smoky margarita: Fandango mezcal with orange liqueur, blood orange, fresh lime and a touch of salt. It's for margarita lovers who want something bolder, with a smoky edge.
c-brasa-roja-mezcal.say: Brasa-Roja: BRAH-sah ROH-hah (Spanish for 'red embers'); Mezcal: mez-KAHL; Cointreau: KWAN-troh
c-brasa-roja-mezcal.taste: Smoky and tangy, with sweet-tart blood orange, sharp lime and a salty finish.

explain.means: A Mexican spirit made from agave, the same family of plants as tequila, known for its smoky taste.
A clear French orange liqueur that adds sweetness and orange flavour, as in a classic margarita.
A sweet syrup made from blood orange, a red-fleshed orange with a slightly berry-like taste.
A classic made with agave spirit, orange liqueur and lime; this one swaps in mezcal for a smoky version.

dishes.why: The smoky mezcal matches the smoky, spicy chorizo, and the lime cuts its richness.
Smoke meets smoke, and the tangy lime stands up to the spicy potatoes.

alts.when: no smoke, fruitier and sweeter
smoky but stronger, with Scotch whisky instead of mezcal

qs.q: What is the base spirit in the Brasa-Roja Mezcal?
qs.why: The Brasa-Roja Mezcal is built on Fandango Mezcal.

qs.q: How would you describe the taste of the Brasa-Roja Mezcal to a guest?
opts: Smoky and tangy, with blood orange, lime and a touch of salt
Sweet and fruity, with raspberry and agave and no smoke
Bittersweet and tropical, with pineapple, lifted by bubbles
Strong and spirit-forward, with gin, Campari and sweet vermouth
qs.why: Mezcal brings the smoke, blood orange syrup and lime make it sweet-tart, and salt finishes it.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Brasa-Roja Mezcal?
qs.why: Blood orange syrup is on the Brasa-Roja Mezcal's list; the others belong to other cocktails.

qs.q: What gives the Brasa-Roja Mezcal its smoky taste?
qs.why: Mezcal is known for its smoky flavour, and Fandango Mezcal is the base of this drink.

qs.q: A guest who loves a margarita but wants something smoky asks what to order. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Brasa-Roja Mezcal is a margarita made with smoky mezcal.

qs.q: What is the difference between the Brasa-Roja Mezcal and the Red Velvet?
opts: The Brasa-Roja Mezcal has mezcal and blood orange syrup; the Red Velvet has blanco tequila, raspberry syrup and agave
The Brasa-Roja Mezcal has blanco tequila and raspberry syrup; the Red Velvet has mezcal and blood orange syrup
The Brasa-Roja Mezcal has no Cointreau; the Red Velvet has Cointreau
The Brasa-Roja Mezcal has black salt and agave; the Red Velvet has plain salt and blood orange
qs.why: Both margaritas have Cointreau and salt, but the Brasa-Roja is smoky mezcal with blood orange, and the Red Velvet is blanco tequila with raspberry.

c-red-velvet.pitch: The Red Velvet is a fruity margarita: El Tequileño blanco tequila with raspberry, orange liqueur, a little agave sweetness and black salt. It's great for guests who like their margaritas on the sweeter, berry side, with no smoke and no bitterness.
c-red-velvet.say: El Tequileño: el teh-kee-LEN-yoh; Blanco: BLAHN-koh; Cointreau: KWAN-troh; Agave: ah-GAH-vay
c-red-velvet.taste: Sweet raspberry and orange over smooth blanco tequila, with a salty edge from black salt.

explain.means: Clear, unaged tequila, made from the agave plant, with a fresh, clean taste.
A clear French orange liqueur that adds sweetness and orange flavour, as in a classic margarita.
A sweetener made from the same plant tequila comes from, which adds a smooth sweetness.
Salt that is black in colour; it adds the salty touch that balances the sweet fruit.

dishes.why: The sweet raspberry and salt match the spicy, sweet and salty flavours of the pizza.
The fruity sweetness cools the spice, and the salt matches the salty fried squid.

alts.when: something smoky
same tequila but more bittersweet, with Campari

qs.q: What is the base spirit in the Red Velvet?
qs.why: The Red Velvet is built on El Tequileño Blanco, which is a blanco tequila.

qs.q: How would you describe the taste of the Red Velvet to a guest?
opts: Sweet and fruity, with raspberry and orange and a salty edge, no smoke
Smoky and tangy, with blood orange, lime and a touch of salt
Bittersweet and tropical, with pineapple, lifted by bubbles
Strong and spirit-forward, with smoky Scotch and honey
qs.why: Raspberry syrup, agave and Cointreau make it sweet and fruity, black salt adds the salty edge, and blanco tequila means no smoke.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Red Velvet?
qs.why: Agave is on the Red Velvet's list; the others belong to other cocktails.

qs.q: In the Red Velvet, which ingredient gives the main berry flavour?
qs.why: House raspberry syrup is the fruit in the Red Velvet; Chambord, strawberry syrup and blood orange syrup are in other cocktails.

qs.q: A guest wants a sweet, fruity margarita with no smoke and no bitterness. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Red Velvet is a blanco tequila margarita with raspberry and agave, with no smoky mezcal and no bitter Campari.

qs.q: What is the difference between the Red Velvet and the Brasa-Roja Mezcal?
opts: The Red Velvet has blanco tequila, raspberry syrup and agave; the Brasa-Roja Mezcal has smoky mezcal and blood orange syrup
The Red Velvet has mezcal and blood orange syrup; the Brasa-Roja Mezcal has blanco tequila and raspberry syrup
The Red Velvet has no Cointreau; the Brasa-Roja Mezcal has Cointreau
The Red Velvet has plain salt and lime juice; the Brasa-Roja Mezcal has black salt and agave
qs.why: Both margaritas have Cointreau and salt, but the Red Velvet is fruity blanco tequila with raspberry, and the Brasa-Roja is smoky mezcal with blood orange.

c-costa-coco.pitch: The Costa Coco is our tropical margarita: Patrón Blanco tequila with orange liqueur, sweet pineapple and rich coconut, plus a salty chili-lime kick from Tajín. It's perfect for anyone who loves a piña colada vibe but still wants the bite of a tequila margarita.
c-costa-coco.say: Costa Coco: KOH-stah KOH-koh; Patrón: pah-TRONE; Cointreau: KWAHN-troh; Tajín: tah-HEEN
c-costa-coco.taste: Sweet and tropical, with pineapple and coconut over clean tequila and a little salty, spicy, limey kick.

explain.means: A clear French orange liqueur that adds sweet orange flavour, the classic orange part of a margarita.
A sweet pineapple syrup that gives the drink its juicy, tropical pineapple flavour.
Coconut cooked down so its flavour is thicker and stronger, giving the drink a rich, creamy coconut taste.
A Mexican seasoning of chili, lime and salt that adds a salty, gently spicy, tangy kick.

dishes.why: The sweet pineapple and coconut cool down the spicy, salty fried squid, and the Tajín picks up on the heat.
Smoky, spicy chorizo loves a sweet, tropical drink that softens the heat.

alts.when: no tequila, but still pineapple and coconut
wants a smoky margarita instead of a tropical one

qs.q: What is the base spirit in the Costa Coco?
qs.why: The Costa Coco is built on Patrón Blanco, an unaged tequila.

qs.q: Which description of the Costa Coco would you give a guest?
opts: Smoky and tart, with blood orange and a salty edge
Bitter, strong and stirred, with no fruit at all
Sweet and tropical, with pineapple and coconut over tequila and a chili-lime kick
Light, dry and bubbly, with lemon and sparkling wine
qs.why: Pineapple cordial and coconut reduction make it sweet and tropical, and Tajín adds the chili-lime kick.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Costa Coco?
qs.why: Coconut reduction is in the Costa Coco; the others belong to the Brasa-Roja Mezcal and the Red Velvet.

qs.q: What does the Tajín bring to the Costa Coco?
opts: A salty, gently spicy chili-lime kick
qs.why: Tajín is a Mexican seasoning of chili, lime and salt.

qs.q: A guest who loves margaritas wants one that tastes tropical, with pineapple and coconut. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Costa Coco is the margarita with pineapple cordial and coconut reduction; La Vita Colada is a rum drink, not a margarita.

qs.q: Both the Costa Coco and the Red Velvet are blanco tequila margaritas with Cointreau. How are they different?
opts: The Costa Coco uses mezcal, and the Red Velvet uses tequila
The Costa Coco has no Cointreau, and the Red Velvet does
The Costa Coco has raspberry syrup and black salt, and the Red Velvet has pineapple cordial and Tajín
The Costa Coco has pineapple cordial, coconut reduction and Tajín, and the Red Velvet has raspberry syrup, agave and black salt
qs.why: The Costa Coco goes tropical with pineapple and coconut, while the Red Velvet is fruity with raspberry and black salt.

c-sangria-blanca.pitch: The Sangria Blanca is our white wine sangria: Chardonnay-Chenin blanc with brandy, orange liqueur and peach liqueur, topped with Sprite. It's light, fruity and easy to drink, great for anyone who prefers white wine or wants something refreshing.
c-sangria-blanca.say: Sangria Blanca: san-GREE-ah BLAHN-kah; Chardonnay: SHAR-doh-nay; Chenin blanc: SHEH-nin BLAHN; St. Rémy: san RAY-mee; Cointreau: KWAHN-troh; Giffard Pêche: zhee-FAR PESH
c-sangria-blanca.taste: Light, fruity and fairly sweet, like white wine with peach and orange and a lemon-lime fizz.

explain.means: A white wine made from two grapes, Chardonnay and Chenin blanc, which is the base of this sangria.
A French brandy; VSOP means it has been aged longer, and it adds warmth and a little depth to the wine.
A clear French orange liqueur that adds sweet orange flavour.
A French peach liqueur that gives the sangria its sweet, juicy peach flavour.

dishes.why: Light, fruity white sangria suits the delicate, herby fried sea bass without overpowering it.
The peach and citrus are lovely with tangy, creamy goat cheese.

alts.when: wants peach flavour in a bubbly spritz instead of a sangria
prefers red wine

qs.q: What are the base alcohols in the Sangria Blanca?
opts: Malbec and St. Rémy VSOP brandy
Chardonnay-Chenin blanc and St. Rémy VSOP brandy
Cabernet Sauvignon and St. Rémy VSOP brandy
qs.why: The Sangria Blanca is built on a Chardonnay-Chenin blanc white wine with St. Rémy VSOP brandy.

qs.q: Which description of the Sangria Blanca would you give a guest?
opts: Deep and bold red wine with berries, and no fizz
Smoky and tart, with a salty edge
Light, fruity and fairly sweet, with white wine, peach and a lemon-lime fizz
qs.why: White wine, peach liqueur, orange liqueur and Sprite make it light, fruity and sweet.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Sangria Blanca?
qs.why: Giffard Pêche, a peach liqueur, is in the Sangria Blanca; Chambord is in the red sangrias.

qs.q: What does the Giffard Pêche add to the Sangria Blanca?
qs.why: Giffard Pêche is a French peach liqueur.

qs.q: A guest wants a sangria but prefers white wine to red. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Sangria Blanca is the only sangria made with white wine.

qs.q: How is the Sangria Blanca different from the Sangria Rosa?
opts: The Sangria Blanca has no Sprite, and the Sangria Rosa does
The Sangria Blanca uses white wine and peach liqueur, and the Sangria Rosa uses Malbec and Chambord
The Sangria Blanca uses brandy, and the Sangria Rosa has none
The Sangria Blanca uses Cabernet Sauvignon, and the Sangria Rosa uses Chardonnay
qs.why: Both have brandy, Cointreau and Sprite, but the Blanca is white wine with peach, while the Rosa is Malbec with black raspberry.

c-sangria-rosa.pitch: The Sangria Rosa is a juicy red wine sangria: Malbec with brandy, orange liqueur, black raspberry liqueur and grapefruit, topped with Sprite. It's fruity with a tart edge and a little fizz, great for red wine lovers who want something lighter and more refreshing.
c-sangria-rosa.say: Sangria Rosa: san-GREE-ah ROH-sah; Malbec: MAL-bek; St. Rémy: san RAY-mee; Cointreau: KWAHN-troh; Chambord: sham-BOR
c-sangria-rosa.taste: Juicy red wine with raspberry and orange, a tart grapefruit edge and a light lemon-lime fizz.

explain.means: A red wine known for dark, plummy fruit, which is the base of this sangria.
A French brandy; VSOP means it has been aged longer, and it adds warmth and depth to the wine.
A clear French orange liqueur that adds sweet orange flavour.
A French black raspberry liqueur that adds sweet, rich berry flavour.

dishes.why: Fruity red wine with a tart grapefruit edge is great with salty cured meats and cheese.
The juicy red fruit stands up to the rich, savoury braised pork meatballs.

alts.when: wants a bolder red sangria with no soda
prefers white wine

qs.q: What are the base alcohols in the Sangria Rosa?
opts: Chardonnay-Chenin blanc and St. Rémy VSOP brandy
Malbec and St. Rémy VSOP brandy
Cabernet Sauvignon and St. Rémy VSOP brandy
qs.why: The Sangria Rosa is built on Malbec red wine with St. Rémy VSOP brandy.

qs.q: Which description of the Sangria Rosa would you give a guest?
opts: Juicy red wine with raspberry, a tart grapefruit edge and a light fizz
Light white wine with peach and lots of sweetness
Strong, bitter and stirred, with no fruit
qs.why: Malbec, Chambord, grapefruit and Sprite make it juicy, a little tart and lightly fizzy.

qs.q: Which of these is in the Sangria Rosa?
qs.why: Grapefruit is in the Sangria Rosa and gives it a tart edge.

qs.q: What does the Chambord add to the Sangria Rosa?
qs.why: Chambord is a French black raspberry liqueur.

qs.q: A guest wants a red wine sangria with a little fizz and a tart citrus edge. Which cocktail do you suggest?
qs.why: The Sangria Rosa is the red sangria with grapefruit and Sprite; the Tinta has no Sprite, and the Blanca is white wine.

qs.q: How is the Sangria Rosa different from the Sangria Tinta?
opts: The Sangria Rosa has Chambord, and the Sangria Tinta does not
The Sangria Rosa uses white wine, and the Sangria Tinta uses red
The Sangria Rosa uses Malbec with grapefruit and Sprite, and the Sangria Tinta uses Cabernet Sauvignon with orange and no Sprite
The Sangria Rosa has no brandy, and the Sangria Tinta has St. Rémy
qs.why: Both have brandy, Cointreau and Chambord, but the wine, the fruit and the Sprite are different.

c-sangria-tinta.pitch: The Sangria Tinta is our boldest sangria: Cabernet Sauvignon with brandy, orange liqueur, black raspberry liqueur, citrus and orange. It's rich and fruity, perfect for red wine lovers or anyone eating a hearty meat dish.
c-sangria-tinta.say: Sangria Tinta: san-GREE-ah TEEN-tah; Cabernet Sauvignon: KAB-er-nay SOH-vin-yohn; St. Rémy: san RAY-mee; Cointreau: KWAHN-troh; Chambord: sham-BOR
c-sangria-tinta.taste: Rich, full red wine with warm brandy, black raspberry and orange.

explain.means: A full-bodied red wine with dark fruit flavour, which gives this sangria its bold character.
A French brandy; VSOP means it has been aged longer, and it adds warmth and depth to the wine.
A clear French orange liqueur that adds sweet orange flavour.
A French black raspberry liqueur that adds sweet, rich berry flavour.

dishes.why: A bold red wine sangria stands up to the rich, savoury braised beef sauce.
Full red fruit and brandy match the charred, rich lamb.

alts.when: wants a lighter red sangria with a little fizz
wants red wine flavour in a stronger gin cocktail

qs.q: What are the base alcohols in the Sangria Tinta?
opts: Malbec and St. Rémy VSOP brandy
Chardonnay-Chenin blanc and St. Rémy VSOP brandy
Cabernet Sauvignon and St. Rémy VSOP brandy
qs.why: The Sangria Tinta is built on Cabernet Sauvignon with St. Rémy VSOP brandy; Cabernet with Roku Gin is the Blue Rose.

qs.q: Which description of the Sangria Tinta would you give a guest?
opts: Light white wine with peach and lemon-lime fizz
Rich, full red wine with brandy, black raspberry and orange
Smoky and tart, with blood orange and salt
Bitter and herbal, with gin and vermouth
qs.why: Cabernet Sauvignon, brandy, Chambord and orange make it rich, full and fruity.
